newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - SEPT 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - SEPT 9.

text.p: -- EUROTUNNEL POISED FOR 350 MILLION STG DEFICIT

There is speculation that the outgoing co-chairman of Eurotunnel, Sir Alastair Morton, will on Monday reveal that the company ran up losses of 350 million stg during the first half of 1996. Despite seeing its share of the cross-Channel market rise, the finances of the massive project remain fragile. Talks are continuing between the company and a consortium of banks regarding the financing of its massive debts.
-- WICKES' PROFIT GAP NEARS 50 MILLION STG

Investigations by a number of parties into accounting irregularities at retail chain Wickes are reported to have uncovered a shortfall of some 50 million stg in the company's reported profits over the past three years. Meanwhile, the company's directors have noted that sales at its outlets continue to rise, prompting optimism about its commercial survival. There is speculation that as part of a survival plan the company may embark on a rights issue as well as a series of disposals.
-- MORGAN INVESTORS MAY GET NEW AID

There is speculation that German parent bank Deutsche Bank may extend a financial rescue package being made available to investors in a number of funds that were last week suspended after it was discovered there had been breaches to rules governing investments. A fund manager at the core of the affair, Peter Young, is being investigated, particularly in relation to his own personal finances. It is thought that Deutsche Bank will be looking for resignations from managers involved in supervising Young.
-- EU TO DELAY ACTION AGAINST ANTI-CUBA LAW

Following a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland, the European Commission president Jacques Delors has noted that it may well prove prudent to wait before embarking on retaliation against the United States over laws which will result in foreign companies trading with Cuba facing sanctions. Meanwhile, the Irish foreign minister Dick Spring has announced that a conference will take place in October aimed at rejuvenating the review currently under way of the Maastricht treaty.
-- EUROSTAR SLEEPER TRAINS RUN INTO POWER SUPPLY PROBLEM

It has emerged that concerns about power supply on the British side of the Channel may derail plans by Eurostar to offer sleeper carriages on its Channel Tunnel rail services. A spokesman for the company which operates Eurostar noted that the planned trains, which use a great deal of power, could actually grind to a halt were too many people on board to make use of services that draw power. The addition of sleeper carriages is seen as vital to Eurostar extending its operations beyond the southeast of England.
-- UNIONS URGED TO MOVE TO BINDING ARBITRATION

On the eve of the annual Trades Union Congress gathering in Blackpool the leader of the AEEU, Ken Jackson, has raised the possibility of unions accepting binding arbitration as an alternative means to strikes for resolving industrial disputes. He noted that the adoption of such a strategy could consign strikes to history. Disruption caused by a number of recent strikes in the UK involving rail and postal services have prompted concern within Labour party ranks.
-- TAX CUTS BEHIND PLAN FOR VAT ON TECs, SAYS LABOUR

Labour has revealed that leaked documents prove that plans are afoot to apply a value added tax levy on Britain's training and enterprise councils. The party maintains that such a levy would be used to provide the Treasury with greater scope for cuts in taxes in November's budget, but would also have the effect of reducing the number of training places made available by TECs.
-- SAINSBURY WILL DROP SPURIOUS 'GREEN' PRODUCTS

It is reported that on Monday the UK retailer J. Sainsbury will announce that it is to discontinue a range of cleaning products that are claimed to be environmentally sound. The move comes in the wake of a report from the National Consumer Council (NCC) which reveals that some of the claims made of the items are spurious. Sainsbury undertook a review of its Greencare of household cleaning products after the NCC found that some offered no environmental advantage over standard alternatives.
-- WHITE GOODS SALES 'SET FOR HIGH GROWTH'

Sales of domestic appliances in the UK are forecast by two of the sector's leading players, Electrolux and Hotpoint, to rise sharply this year. Improvements in consumer confidence and the housing market are seen as central to the anticipated increases in sales of washing machines, fridges and other home appliances. However, while volume sales are expected to increase, competition in the market means that the total value will remain more or less static.
-- INDUSTRY PRESSES ON VAT CLAIMS

The Confederation of British Industry is reported to have approached the European Commission in an attempt to determine whether or not proposals for limiting the reclaiming by UK companies of wrongly paid value-added tax are in fact in breach of EU laws. The CBI is also believed to have made its case about the unfairness of the proposals directly to the Chancellor of the Exchequer. It is planned that a three-year time limit will be placed on companies claiming back VAT which they should not have paid in the first instance.
